column1: # PROVENANCE AND FETCH MAP for the canonical vectors. Data, not prose:
# docrender/vectors.py READS this file on every build, twice -- once to find
# each vector UPSTREAM, and once to compare hashes.
# WHAT CHANGED ON 2026-08-06, AND WHY THIS HEADER IS A RETRACTION
# This file used to open with a warning that it could not answer the question
# anybody actually had:
#   STRUCK: "DOES NOT PROVE: that what we vendored is still current upstream.
#   That needs a scheduled job with network access, and it does not exist yet."
# Michael: "the renderer should pull from canonical; there should be no
# in-between. why is this happening?" The honest answer was that nobody ever
# decided it -- the first extraction copied the files in to get moving, and
# three separate commits then improved the PROSE about the gap instead of
# closing it. It ate his own typography and spacing edits on 08-05: fifty
# minutes live upstream and absent from every site, found only because somebody
# read this log for an unrelated reason.
# THE ENGINE NOW READS THESE VECTORS LIVE, per file, per build:
#   the design system was checked out and the file is there  ->  LIVE
#   anything else                                            ->  the copy in
#                                                                this folder,
#                                                                reported LOUDLY
# THE `path` COLUMN IS EXECUTABLE NOW. IT USED TO BE A NOTE.
# It recorded where each file came from, for a human reading the table. It is
# now what vectors.py joins on to find the file upstream -- so a wrong value no
# longer merely misleads a reader, it silently falls THAT FILE back to the
# vendored copy while its neighbours stay live.
# The column did not change shape. Its cost of being wrong did. That mixed state
# is reported by name, because live colours joined to a vendored join table can
# point at a row that no longer exists -- and the symptom otherwise arrives as a
# dangling pointer with no stated cause.
# A FILE ABSENT FROM THIS TABLE IS NEVER FETCHED. `aliases.tsv` and `bridge.tsv`
# live in this folder and are OURS -- they join this engine's vocabulary to the
# design system's and have no upstream. They are not listed here, so the
# resolver never looks for them. Nothing in the code knows their names.
# WHAT THE HASH PROVES NOW
# LIVE PATH: that the file fetched IS the one recorded here. A mismatch is NOT a
# defect -- it means upstream has moved since the last re-vendor, which is the
# normal state of a live read. What it costs is the FALLBACK: if the design
# system were unreachable right now, this site would paint the older bytes. So
# it prints a note asking for a re-vendor, and the build carries on.
# FALLBACK PATH: the old meaning, unchanged. The file on disk is not what was
# recorded, so somebody edited it in place or the copy is damaged. That one is
# reported as a real defect, because it is the file actually being rendered.
# THE RECORDED HASHES ARE THEREFORE THE FALLBACK'S PROVENANCE, not the site's.
# A smaller job than they used to have, and still worth doing: a stale fallback
# is harmless until the day the fetch fails, which is the worst possible day to
# find out.
# WHY THE VENDORED FILES CARRY NO HEADER COMMENTS
# Every other TSV in this engine opens with a comment block. These do not, and
# that is deliberate: a comment would change their bytes and destroy the one
# thing that proves they ARE the canonical tables. Their identity is their hash.
# HOW TO REFRESH: replace the file wholesale from the source repo, put the new
# blob SHA here, and re-run the build. Never edit a vendored file in place.
# REFRESH LOG. Newest first.
# KEPT IN FULL, deliberately, now that it no longer describes the only way
# values reach a site. Every entry records what changed upstream and why, and
# several carry measurements that exist nowhere else -- the amber decided by the
# marker chip rather than the page, the four occurrences of identical byte counts
# with different content, the transposition that made the colour table clueless.
# That is the only history of this design system's decisions the engine holds.
# 2026-10-08  NEW VECTOR frames.tsv, f0b2547, 87 B, 1 row. Sign frames for
#             `type: sign` (specs/sign-layout.md R3, docrender/sign.py), born
#             from Michael's CAST AND CREW ONLY sign (maw-themes PR #17). The
#             one row is three nested bands in sheet points: outer red 13 (the
#             URITP logo red, sampled from the source PDF -- NOT a UR brand
#             colour), middle URochester Navy 13, inner Dandelion Yellow 8 --
#             both from the 2025 UR brand guide, which REPLACED the 2010
#             PMS 541 / 109 the source sign was printed in. Vendored and
#             upstream are the same blob, verified by content address.
#             ⚠️ Not a theme property: no join points at it. A page names a row
#             directly with `frame:`, so vectors.known() never reads this file.
# 2026-09-28  DEPARTMENT THEMES, AND ALL FIVE FALLBACKS CAUGHT UP IN ONE PASS.
#             themes.json 7711cab -> 46d4c2a, 12 -> 21 joins. typography
#             5f6ec2d -> ef00399, forms 9433b6a -> 5b78645, spacing
#             a4996d0 -> 7345616. Michael: six per-page department themes,
#             dept-scenic / -sm / -audio / -video / -admin / -lx (maw-themes
#             PR #14). Each is the black-ground stage look with ONE accent band
#             swapped; the colour rows are dept-<x>-dark / -light so that no
#             new slug is both a join and a colour -- the bare-name ambiguity
#             this build already warns about for one pre-existing slug is not
#             multiplied by six. Same pass: that slug's colour rows got
#             legible text-faint and a black on-accent (was 1.4:1 and 2.3:1).
#             THE JOIN FALLBACK WAS 54 DAYS STALE AND MISSING TWO LIVE JOINS,
#             plus a typography, forms and spacing entity each. The 08-19 lesson
#             one file over: a stale fallback shrinks the legal theme set, and
#             this one would have dropped a live site's declared theme on the
#             first failed checkout. It also never matched its own recorded
#             hash -- somebody had prepended a PROJECTION note in place. Replaced
#             wholesale; it is now upstream's bytes and nothing else.
#             VERIFIED BY CONTENT ADDRESS: all five SHAs below were computed
#             from the bytes pushed here and equal maw-themes main.
# 2026-08-19  THE FALLBACK WENT FOURTEEN DAYS STALE AND NOBODY NOTICED, WHICH IS
#             THE ENTRY. colors 003fb9c -> e3819e3, 7,777 -> 8,433 B,
#             39 -> 41 rows. TWO separate upstream changes arrived in ONE
#             re-vendor because nothing refreshes this folder automatically and
#             the live read made the gap invisible.
#             (a) `link` is now authored on ALL 41 rows. It was authored on TWO
#             when it was vendored on 08-05 (see the entry below), and the note
#             in this table still said "blank on 37" -- true on the day it was
#             written and false within days. THE FALLBACK'S OWN DESCRIPTION
#             ROTTED, not just its bytes.
#             (b) NEW ROWS `uritp` and `uritp-light`, which is the half that
#             actually bites. `vectors.known()` reads this table to decide which
#             theme names an instance may legally declare -- so on any build
#             where the maw-themes checkout fails, a site declaring `uritp`
#             resolved to `base` and rendered the nine-token stand-in. A stale
#             fallback does not only paint old colours, IT SHRINKS THE LEGAL
#             THEME SET.
#             Michael's own change in the same pass: papyrus `link` #6e4b2a ->
#             #7b2d8e and papyrus-dark #c59468 -> #d38ce8 (maw-themes PR #12).
#             The old values were not wrong, they were in the WRONG FAMILY --
#             the same brown as `accent` one shade deeper, so a link on
#             parchment read as emphasis. Violet is the one unoccupied hue in
#             both rows. Explicitly reversible; he asked for it that way.
#             VERIFIED BY CONTENT ADDRESS rather than by inspection: the
#             vendored blob SHA is e3819e37, IDENTICAL to upstream's, which is
#             git proving the two files are the same bytes. That is the check to
#             use every time this folder is refreshed -- it is free and it is
#             the only one that cannot be fooled by a plausible-looking diff.
# 2026-08-05  A LINK IS ITS OWN ROLE. colors 579bb57 -> 003fb9c, 24 -> 25
#             columns: NEW `link`, authored on eos (#c495b5) and eos-light
#             (#8a4374) and BLANK on the other 37 rows. Michael: "change the
#             color that LINKS use to be not in the same family as note, active,
#             and sticky columns... is there a free or better color column to
#             use?" Measured answer: there was not one. accent-deep is 2 deg
#             from accent and info is 12 -- same family, would read as a mistake;
#             accent-2 is genuinely distinct but already letters @term: links, so
#             a real link would become indistinguishable from a span that is not
#             clickable; good/warn/bad each already mean something a link does
#             not; data-1..4 are byte-identical in all 39 rows. Hue 319 is the
#             one unoccupied region. WARNING a blank cell is not emitted, so
#             `var(--dr-link, var(--dr-accent))` keeps all 37 other themes
#             rendering byte-identically.
# 2026-08-05  MICHAEL'S OWN EDITS, VENDORED ~50 MIN LATE. THE INCIDENT THAT
#             EVENTUALLY KILLED VENDORING ALTOGETHER (see the header).
#             typography cbf0c9e -> 5f6ec2d: eos display 'Chakra Petch' ->
#             'Archivo', mono 'JetBrains Mono' -> 'IBM Plex Mono'. spacing
#             a355d55 -> a4996d0: eos pad-cell 6->3px, pad-card 12->8px, gap-md
#             10->6px, gap-lg 20->12px, roughly halving all four.
#             THE SPACING EDIT IS VISIBLE AND THE TYPOGRAPHY ONE IS NOT.
#             Nothing in this engine fetches a webfont -- `theme.font` is never
#             set in mkdocs.yml -- so a font NAME changes and no file is
#             requested, and 'Archivo' falls through to system-ui. The type
#             vector's three font columns have never rendered on any site. Full
#             write-up in assets/type.css. STILL OPEN: reading the vectors live
#             fixes the DELAY, not the missing webfont loader.
# 2026-08-05  EOS-LIGHT JOINS THE CONSOLE. colors 4691aee -> 579bb57. Michael:
#             "fix the eos light theme to now fit the same muted blue
#             aesthetics? could do for more notable amber pops in both of them."
#             14 cells on eos-light, 1 on eos dark. The light row was still from
#             the proof era -- violet chrome, 100%-sat magenta accent, electric
#             blue accent-2 -- so the pair had a violet half and a blue half.
#             Chrome now 215.0-216.9, a 1.9 degree spread against the dark row's
#             2.8 at 216; accent matched in HUE (212.0 vs 212.7) and separated
#             in weight. THE AMBER WAS DECIDED BY THE MARKER CHIP, not by
#             the page: `warn` paints the confidence box, whose text sits on a
#             10% wash of ITSELF, and three more saturated candidates cleared
#             the page while failing that. 7,719 B before and after --
#             FOURTH occurrence on this file.
# 2026-08-05  THE EOS HARNESS RETIRES. colors c576bcf -> 4691aee, themes.json
#             e6b7c7e -> 7711cab. Michael: "i think i've proved my point with
#             the eos wild themes... revert the one color row to a more stable
#             'eos' blind mode blue and yellow and blue and purple." 22 of 24
#             cells on the eos DARK row, re-authored from a photograph of an
#             Element2 console sitting in BLIND; every chrome cell now lands
#             within THREE degrees of hue 217 where the harness spanned 224.
#             themes.json carries prose only -- the eos join's harness warning
#             was now false and the semantic grammar is stated instead.
#             colors.tsv is 7,719 B BEFORE AND AFTER. Third occurrence
#             in this file of identical size with different content.
# 2026-08-05  THE COLOUR TABLE BECOMES CLUELESS. colors 75b3f6c -> c576bcf
#             (38 cols -> 24, 23 rows -> 39), themes.json 09e429b -> e6b7c7e
#             (schemaVersion 4, +alt-color on every join).
#             Michael: "the color tab needs to be totally clueless as to its
#             joins to any other state... any joining must happen externally in
#             a join table." CULLED identity, name and the 12-column alt- band;
#             every alt band TRANSPOSED into its own complete row (williams-dark,
#             ferrari-light, papyrus-dark...) losslessly, since the 7 tokens the
#             band never carried were SHARED and already painted into both
#             schemes. The engine cannot read this table without the matching
#             vectors.py commit -- derivation reads a column that no longer
#             exists. And the first write was REFUSED on a stale SHA:
#             Michael had hand-committed an eos identification harness minutes
#             earlier (9374be2) and the generated table would have wiped it.
# 2026-08-05  667e4a9 -> 75b3f6c  OUTLANDISH ACCENTS, 30 cells across the six
#             split rows. Deliberate PROOF VALUES: Material's fallback blue
#             survived for weeks because it read as "docs site" rather than as
#             broken. All measured against canvas AND card AND their own
#             on-accent; two candidates rejected on measurement (4.44, 4.36).
#             SAME 6,674 BYTES as the previous vendor.
# 2026-08-05  e14e3a6 -> 667e4a9  THE SPLIT. J10/S1 implemented for three
#             identities. This broke `light: eos` in site.yml SILENTLY.
# 2026-08-05  eade05c -> e14e3a6  eos light: placeholder green retired, magenta
#             deepened for the light ground (3.46:1 -> 5.06:1).
# 2026-08-05  27b5327 -> eade05c  eos dark RE-AUTHORED; amber moves to `accent`,
#             on-accent inverts to near-black, clearing eos from D7.
# 2026-08-05  4f391aa -> 27b5327  ONE CELL, a proof value. STILL 5,710 BYTES --
#             the argument for hashing over measuring.
# 2026-08-04  --      -> 4f391aa  Initial vendor. 19 themes x 36 columns.

canonical/colors.tsv
column7: 55 rows x 25 columns. One row is ONE COMPLETE PALETTE and the table expresses no relationship of any kind -- no identity, no alt- band. `mode` is descriptive only. `link` is authored on EVERY row. Twelve dept-<x>-dark/-light rows arrived 09-28 -- vectors.known() reads this table, so a stale copy here also shrinks the set of theme names an instance may legally declare.

column1: canonical/themes.json
column7: THE JOIN, schemaVersion 4. 21 themes, FIVE pointers each: color, alt-color, typography, forms, spacing. Pairing lives here and nowhere else. A new COLOUR column moves no pointer, so this file does not change when one is added. Upstream's bytes exactly -- no projection note, which is what broke the hash before 09-28.

column1: canonical/typography.tsv
column7: 7 SHARED entities on their own slugs. Joined by pointer -- editing one moves every theme pointing at it. WARNING the three FONT columns do not render: nothing in this engine fetches a webfont. See assets/type.css.

column1: canonical/forms.tsv
column7: 6 SHARED entities. Radii, border weight, gradient angle, shadows, elevation, motion.

column1: canonical/spacing.tsv
column7: 7 SHARED entities. Touch target, cell and card padding, three gaps.
